spanish: O el que exhorta, *que lo haga* en la exhortación; el que comparte, *que lo haga* con generosidad; el que dirige, *que lo haga* con diligencia; el que muestra misericordia, *que lo haga* con alegría.

adjudication.decision: **Razones de la traducción** - «O» continues the enumeration introduced by εἴτε. - Each expression «el que…» represents an article followed by a substantivized participle. - The Greek clauses contain no equivalent of «que lo haga»; therefore, all four occurrences must remain italicized. - «El que exhorta… en la exhortación» preserves the deliberate repetition παρακαλῶν / παρακλήσει. - «Comparte» translates μεταδιδούς as sharing or giving to others. - In a context of sharing, ἁπλότης naturally expresses openhandedness or generosity. «Sencillez» preserves its basic lexical sense but may sound as though the manner of sharing should merely be uncomplicated. - «El que dirige» represents προϊστάμενος without specifying a particular office. - «Con diligencia» preserves ἐν σπουδῇ and its sense of diligence, zeal, or earnestness. - «Muestra misericordia» translates ἐλεῶν. - «Con alegría» represents ἐν ἱλαρότητι, the cheerful disposition with which mercy is shown.
